tidyllm - Developer / Coding-Agent Guide

Source: claude.md

tidyllm is a tidy, functional interface to large language model APIs in R (0.6.0 on CRAN since 2026-09-08; 0.7.0 in development). Everything is verb(.llm, provider()): chat(), send_chat(), parallel_chat(), embed(), send_batch(), the job and remote-file verbs. Fourteen providers implement a shared set of S7 generics declared in R/APIProvider.R. It targets data pipelines, batch work and provider-specific power features; ellmer targets interactive agents and Shiny. The two are complementary. Architecture, the provider matrix, the media system, the async design and the roadmap live in the wiki (below); this file is the map.

File layout (R/)

File or prefix Role
APIProvider.R Provider base class and every generic. Read this before adding a provider.
llm_verbs.R Verb dispatch, dispatch_to_provider(), create_provider_function()
LLMMessage.R, llm_message.R The immutable message class and its constructor
chat_pipeline.R The build / perform / finish split every provider chat goes through
stream_pump.R One shared streaming pump; parse_stream_event() dispatch
async_chat.R, parallel_chat.R send_chat() on R’s event loop; parallel_chat() over req_perform_parallel()
media.R The five media S7 classes and their constructors
tools.R, tidyllm_schema.R The TOOL class and the JSON schema system
message_retrieval.R get_reply(), get_metadata(), get_reply_data()
perform_api_requests.R, rate_limits.R, embedding_helpers.R, pdfbatch.R, utilites.R Shared machinery (utilites.R is spelled that way; historical)
api_chat_completions.R The ChatCompletions base class, shared by seven providers
api_openai.R The OpenAI Responses API; extends APIProvider directly, not ChatCompletions
api_*.R One file per provider: claude, claude_cli, gemini, ollama, mistral, groq, perplexity, deepseek, voyage, azure_openai, openrouter, llamacpp, ellmer
example_app.R tidyllm_example_app(), the Shiny model-explorer demo

DESCRIPTION’s Collate: is hand-maintained: a new or renamed file needs a manual entry, and class definitions must precede the files with methods on them.

Key principles

  • S7 throughout, and S7 is not S4 or R6. Consult the S7 documentation before changing S7 code; most models know S7 badly.
  • A provider’s chat function is the authoritative statement of what that provider supports. create_provider_function() reads its formals via provider(.called_from = "metadata") and filters the verb’s common arguments down to them, which is why chat(openai(), .thinking = TRUE) correctly errors.
  • Message objects are immutable. Inline media lives in message$media, remote file references in message$files, and a tidyllm_file belongs to one provider only.
  • Internal arguments are prefixed with a dot. Validation goes through validate_inputs() with the named-vector pattern: c("Error msg" = cond1, "Other msg" = cond2) |> validate_inputs().
  • All tabular output is a tibble. Functions stay pure; the only global state is .tidyllm_rate_limit_env.
  • The public API is additive. Deprecate with a warning (.imagefile, .pdf, .file_ids), never remove.
  • Runtime dependencies are budgeted at 18 Imports:, currently 17. A new one needs a wiki decision entry. Feature dependencies go in Suggests and are checked at their use site, as later and promises are.

Testing policy

  • Live, non-mocked local tests are the preferred kind. They live in local_tests/: providers/ has one suite per provider, features/ has opt-in suites for paid, stateful or slow features. Read local_tests/results/latest_run.json after every significant change, not at the end.
  • tests/testthat/ must stay CRAN-safe and offline: httptest2 shape checks plus structural tests that need no network.
  • Do not add mocking-based tests without asking first.
  • Run source("local_tests/features/stream_replay.R") after any change to a streaming path. It replays recorded wire bytes through the real handle_stream() and needs no API key.
  • webfakes and other local-test-only packages stay out of DESCRIPTION.
  • browser() cannot be driven from an agent session. Debug post-mortem from local_tests/debug_state/<test>.rda.

Working rules (maintainer feedback)

  • No em-dashes anywhere in prose, roxygen or vignettes. Use a semicolon, a comma apposition, or a colon in a definition list.
  • No code comments unless asked for. No trailing summaries after tool calls.
  • Docs voice is plain and problem-first; a help page should not require knowing the word “dispatch” or reading a file path. README is the pkgdown home page.
  • Commit messages carry no co-author or attribution lines.
  • claude.md and local_context/ are gitignored. Never stage either.
  • perplexity() cannot be live-tested here (no credits; use .dry_run) and azure_openai() cannot be tested at all (no access).

Local folders (untracked)

  • local_context/wiki/ the agent-facing memory (below).
  • local_context/notes/ dated journal entries.
  • local_context/legacy/ the pre-wiki planning notes, bug log, proof-of-concept scripts and superseded vignettes; indexed in wiki note 07. Read-only history.
  • local_context/presentation/, media/, test_data/, llm_cache/ assets.
  • local_tests/, docs/, pkgdown/ stay where they are.

Project memory (llmwiki)

  • Wiki root: local_context/wiki
  • Journal: local_context/notes
  • Kind: software
  • Sweep cutoff: 2026-09-16
  • Schema + workflows: /llmwiki skill.
  • Read local_context/wiki/00_state.md first in every session. Open numbered notes on demand via its pointers; do not re-derive settled design.
  • Before touching design: check local_context/wiki/contentions.md; never silently resolve an open contention, and never sit on a ripe one: close brings contentions whose resolve-condition is met (or which 3 sessions have not moved) back to the user with a recommendation.
  • Corrections: edit the owning note FIRST and stamp it (<!-- swept: anchor date -->), then the register line as receipt (Affects: [[NN_note#anchor]]).
  • Session end / before compact: run /llmwiki close; first thing after a /clear, run /llmwiki next to pick up 00_state.md’s Next list.
  • Artefacts that land (batch runs, recorded fixtures, exports) can nag until the wiki has them: /llmwiki trigger sets one, close discharges it.
  • Run /llmwiki lint after: design adoption/supersession, a release, CLAUDE.md edits, or 5+ sessions without one.
